stem: A media company runs workloads across 40 AWS accounts under AWS Organizations, and different teams have applied inconsistent DataClassification tag values on their S3 buckets, making it impossible to scope an audit by sensitivity. Which action enforces one standard set of tag keys and values across every account?

choices.text: Publish an AWS Organizations tag policy that defines the allowed DataClassification values and enforces compliance on S3 buckets
Ask each account's bucket owner to manually update their bucket policy to include the correct tag
Create an AWS Config rule that only reports which buckets have noncompliant tags, without correcting them
Apply an AWS Organizations service control policy that denies the s3:PutObject action across every member account unless some resource tag is already present on the request

rationale: An AWS Organizations tag policy defines the tag keys and the specific values (such as the approved DataClassification values) that are compliant across every account in the organization, which is exactly the standardization this scenario needs. Asking each bucket owner to update their policy by hand does not standardize anything centrally and leaves the process dependent on manual follow-up across 40 accounts. An AWS Config rule can continuously report which buckets carry a noncompliant tag, but by itself it only flags drift after the fact; it does not define or publish the standard values the way a tag policy does. A service control policy can require that some tag be present before an API call succeeds, but it has no way to define or enforce which tag values count as compliant, so it cannot standardize the DataClassification values themselves.
